name: Men's CAP dark blue polo, short sleeves, left chest pocket, with medium gray trousers and black belt (embroidery positions only)
size_basis: Silhouette traced from CAPR 39-1 Figure 5.5 (3 March 2020, p.80; base-art/ref_polo_CAPR_fig5-5.png, PDF page 108 rendered at 300 dpi, trace-polo.js: shirt-only mask, left half mirrored, Moore trace, RDP 1.1 px). Scale 0.0309 in per figure pixel: the figure's belt buckle is 64 x 66 px, so 1.98 x 2.04 in at this scale against the 2 in limit of CAPR 39-1 5.3.5 (the figure draws the buckle at the limit), and the armhole-seam width (2 x 9.53 in) equals the men's Class B shirt sheet's (167 px x 0.0474 x 1.2171 = 9.63 in half width), i.e. the same wearer. At this scale the figure's embroidered seal is 2.93 in across, the placket 1.30 x 5.41 in, the pocket 4.17 in wide, the belt 1.79 in. ESTIMATE: the regulation gives no garment dimension and the figure is a schematic drawing. Colours sampled from the figure: shirt #001b52, belt #201a18, trousers #746f6c, skirt #86827e.
landmarks_note: rects are {x,y,w,h} (top-left); polygons are [[x,y]...]; all in user units (0.01 in), origin top-left of the artwork box. The *_slot entries that carry w_in / h_in are {x,y} = the CENTRE of the slot in user units, w_in / h_in in inches. seal_slot: embroidered CAP seal, wearer's RIGHT breast (the picture's left), w_in = the figure-measured seal (2.93 in; the insignia-cap-seal asset is 2.50 in, CAPR 39-1 Fig A6-4: the figure draws the polo seal larger, the engine places the asset at the slot centre). pen_pocket_slot: the tactical polo's pen pocket on the wearer's LEFT sleeve (the picture's right), {x,y} its centre, w_in x h_in its size (1.4 x 5.5 in, estimate), angle_deg the SVG rotate() that turns an upright box onto the sleeve's axis, flap_in the flap depth. name_slot: the embroidered name line on the wearer's LEFT breast, w_in = the pocket width 4.17 rounded to 4.2 in; the name sits above the pocket, as Figure 5.5 draws it (0.53 in clear of the pocket top), h_in = the figure's cap height. badge_slot: centre of the badge / duty title line, h_in 1.14 (the figure's badge), 1/2 in above the name_slot top (CAPR 39-1 5.3.2.1.1; the figure draws 0.65 in), w_in nominal. print_seal_slot: the screen-printed CAP seal (5.3.1.2) on the wearer's LEFT breast, the seal_slot mirrored about the centre line; the men's sheet's pocket group (id pocket) is hidden for the printed polo, which has no pocket or accoutrements (5.3.1.2, 5.3.2.1.2). collar_left / collar_right name the leaf on the PICTURE's left / right (as the Class B sheets do); shoulder_seam_right / left and every anchor named left / right are the WEARER's (right = the picture's left). hat_view {front, back}: where the cap assets hat-baseball-cap-blue and hat-baseball-cap-blue-back sit (their boxes, bottoms 0.25 in below the collar-tip line, the back view 0.5 in to the picture's right of the front); they lie above this artwork box. hat_attach: the collar-tip line on the centre line.

scale.basis: belt buckle 64 x 66 px = the 2 in limit of 5.3.5; same-wearer shoulder width of the Class B shirt

documented: dark blue knit polo shirt, short or long sleeves, embroidered CAP seal on the RIGHT breast, male version with a left-chest pocket (CAPR 39-1 5.3.1.1)

first and last name embroidered in white thread on the LEFT breast (above the pocket, as Figure 5.5 draws it); one badge or duty title 1/2 in over the name; no grade insignia (5.3.1.1, 5.3.2, 5.3.2.1.1)
medium gray trousers, slim, straight or loose (5.3.3); plain black belt with a plain buckle not over 2 in, 2 in wide at most (5.3.5)
assumed: garment dimensions (scale from the 2 in buckle limit and the Class B same-wearer shoulder width)
no photograph of a real CAP polo was available offline (the charter forbids downloads): colours are sampled from Figure 5.5
collar leaf, placket, button, pocket, belt, loop and buckle geometry read off Figure 5.5 (pixel table FIG in make-polo.js)
seams, stitches and the ribbed cuff are shown as flat geometric lines, no knit texture
short sleeve as drawn in Figure 5.5 (it reaches the elbow, longer than a real polo sleeve of about 9 in)
trousers and belt cut off at the sheet crop line, trouser flare continued past the figure's crop at the measured slope
